findings.description: Tapping the reader-mode button now produces readerModeLongPressAction, so BrowserViewController calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction instead of toggleReaderMode. Reader view no longer opens/closes; the page is saved to the reading list instead. On a private tab this also persists its URL and title into the profile's ReadingList.db without a save request. Restore displayView: .readerMode in handleShowReaderModeAction.
findings.failureMode: Ordinary reader-mode taps trigger persistent reading-list writes, including private page URLs and titles, instead of toggling reader view.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode display action for ordinary taps

findings.description: This helper runs before showReaderMode is dispatched, so .available should pass true (opening) and .active should pass false (closing). The existing ToolbarTelemetry mapper puts isEnabled into is_private; reversing these values newly reports private opening taps as non-private and normal closing taps as private. It also breaks the existing nil-state test's isPrivate assertion. Restore .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode telemetry changes previously correct private-mode classifications to their opposites; the existing nil-state test's isPrivate assertion fails.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry polarity

findings.description: With a reader-mode tab selected, cancelling editing or opening the menu/tab tray now dispatches its internal http://localhost:.../reader-mode/page URL. AddressBarState overwrites the decoded article URL, and LocationView displays localhost and fills the next edit with the internal URL. The leaveOverlay path does not decode it again. Restore the reader-mode exclusion so cancelEdit falls back to the already decoded state.url.
findings.failureMode: Reader-view cancellation and menu/tab-tray interactions replace the article address with localhost and expose the internal URL in subsequent address-bar edits.
findings.title: Keep internal reader URLs out of cancelEdit actions

findings.description: Removing private exposes the implementation-only Glean wrapper to the module and leaves the changed property without an explicit access modifier, violating AGENTS.md rule 11. Visible consumers already inject the wrapper through init and never access this property directly. Restore private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: An implementation-only dependency becomes module-accessible instead of satisfying the mandatory explicit, minimal access-control rule.
findings.title: Retain private access for the telemetry dependency

findings.description: The atoms schedules endpoint returns listHandler data unchanged, where Availability.days is Prisma Int[]. Declaring days as string[] makes ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper's getScheduleListItemData(schedule) call fail with TS2345 because that transformer requires number[]. Change days back to number[].
findings.failureMode: The schedule list wrapper's unchanged transformer call now fails TypeScript checking.
findings.title: Keep availability days numeric

findings.description: The original response uses IFromUser.id: number, but the copied SlotInfo declares it as string. This makes useAvailableSlots data incompatible with both BookerPlatformWrapper's schedule prop and EventTypeCalendarViewComponent's useAvailableTimeSlots call (which requires IGetAvailableSlots), producing TS2322. Keep fromUser.id numeric.
findings.failureMode: The available-slots result fails the unchanged Booker and calendar-view schedule contracts.
findings.title: Preserve numeric out-of-office source IDs

findings.description: The new ./booker/types export points to ./booker/types.ts, but the files allowlist only ships dist, globals.min.css, and fonts. Packing and resolving this subpath from the extracted package produces MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Map the export to a shipped declaration entry so installed consumers can import the migrated types.
findings.failureMode: The newly exported types subpath resolves to a file absent from the published package.
findings.title: Publish the target of the new booker types export

findings.description: Moving Slot changes userIds from number[] to string[] while onTimeslotsLoaded still uses this type. An existing callback typed for numeric user IDs is now rejected by TypeScript (TS2322), despite no payload conversion. Restore number[] to preserve the callback contract.
findings.failureMode: Existing numeric-ID onTimeslotsLoaded callback signatures no longer type-check against Booker props.
findings.title: Preserve numeric slot user IDs

findings.description: Calling validateCreateScheduleInput({name: "Work", schedule: {}, eventTypeId: "bad"}) succeeds and returns values that do not satisfy CreateScheduleInput. The existing create schema rejects both fields, and the new validator never checks them or interval start/end Dates. Validate the complete input with a local typed schema before returning it.
findings.failureMode: The new exported validator accepts invalid optional schedule and eventTypeId values as validated input.
findings.title: Validate optional fields before returning a schedule input

findings.description: The broadened error-level rule also bans the existing QueryCell imports in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx:12 and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx:6. Biome now emits noRestrictedImports errors for both, so linting/staging these atoms files fails (SKIP_WARNINGS cannot waive errors). Migrate those imports to an allowed shared/local component before enabling the blanket ban.
findings.failureMode: The new error-level ban rejects two still-used atoms imports and blocks lint/pre-commit on those files.
findings.title: Migrate remaining imports before banning all tRPC paths

findings.description: Calling validateCreateScheduleInput(null) or passing a primitive throws a bare Error with no typed code. Callers cannot identify it as a validation failure without parsing the message, violating the mandatory coded-error contract in AGENTS.md §10. Throw ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode.BadRequest and input context instead.
findings.failureMode: Non-object validation failures expose an uncategorized Error instead of the mandated typed-code error.
findings.title: Use a coded error for non-object schedule inputs

findings.description: Calling validateCreateScheduleInput({name: ""}) throws a bare Error without a typed validation code, so callers must parse its message to classify the failure. This violates AGENTS.md §10 independently of the non-object branch. Use ErrorWithCode with ErrorCode.BadRequest and field context here.
findings.failureMode: Invalid-name validation failures return an uncategorized error rather than the required typed-code error.
findings.title: Use a coded error for invalid schedule names

findings.description: The new 'object' literal uses single quotes while the mandated Biome configuration uses quoteStyle: "double". `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits 1 and flags this line. Use double quotes to satisfy the repository formatting contract.
findings.failureMode: The new validator fails the mandated Biome formatting check at its object-type condition.
findings.title: Format the object-type literal with Biome

findings.description: The new error message is single-quoted rather than following the mandated Biome quoteStyle: "double" configuration. `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits 1 and requires double quotes on this line.
findings.failureMode: The new validator fails the required formatting contract at the non-object error message.
findings.title: Format the non-object error message with Biome

findings.description: This condition uses a single-quoted 'string' literal contrary to the mandated Biome quoteStyle: "double" configuration. The focused `biome format` check exits 1 and flags this line; change the literal to double quotes.
findings.failureMode: The validator's name-type condition is rejected by the repository's formatter.
findings.title: Format the name-type literal with Biome

findings.description: The single-quoted error message deviates from the mandatory Biome quoteStyle: "double" configuration. `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits 1 and identifies this line; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: The validator's invalid-name message fails the required formatter check.
findings.title: Format the invalid-name message with Biome

findings.description: `make type-check` fails here with `reportReturnType`, and Mypy reports the same error: the guard leaves `rendered` typed as `str | None`, but `render_template` declares `-> str`. Remove `rendered is not None and` so None is rejected alongside other non-string results and the adapter satisfies its string contract.
findings.failureMode: The required make type-check exits with reportReturnType at template_renderer.py:40, blocking the backend type-check.
findings.title: Reject None before returning the renderer result

findings.description: The new branch ignores the `node_class` resolved immediately above and always constructs TemplateTransformNode v1. A template-transform implementation registered under another version now receives the wrong implementation/output when a graph requests that version. Preserve the mapped class while injecting the renderer.
findings.failureMode: A registered template-transform v2 node requested via data.version='2' is silently replaced by the v1 TemplateTransformNode, so its renderer and run behavior are not used.
findings.title: Instantiate the selected template node version

findings.description: A valid renderer whose __bool__ returns False (or whose __len__ returns zero) is silently replaced with the CodeExecutor adapter. The injected render_template is never called, and workflow rendering instead uses the sandbox. Test explicitly for None here and in DifyNodeFactory's equivalent fallback at node_factory.py:63.
findings.failureMode: Passing a falsey but protocol-conforming template renderer produces default-sandbox output or sandbox-service errors instead of the injected renderer's output.
findings.title: Do not discard a falsey injected renderer

findings.description: The added reversed assertion triggers SIM300 in the repository's Ruff configuration. `make check` now exits with this error; use `assert result.outputs['output'] == '1, two, 3.0, True'` to satisfy the required lint check.
findings.failureMode: make check fails because the new equality assertion violates enabled Ruff SIM300.
findings.title: Put the actual output on the left of the assertion

findings.description: Repository mandates require Ruff-formatted Python. `ruff format --check` exits 1 for this file, and `ruff format --diff` identifies this new signature as needing to be collapsed onto one line. Apply the formatter to this definition.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory Ruff formatting check exits 1 because the new concatenation test signature is not formatted according to api/.ruff.toml.
findings.title: Apply Ruff formatting to the concatenation test

findings.description: This new signature independently violates the required Ruff formatting. `ruff format --diff` rewrites it onto one line; fixing only the concatenation signature still leaves formatting validation exiting 1. Apply the formatter to this definition too.
findings.failureMode: The new conditional test's signature independently causes Ruff formatting validation to fail.
findings.title: Apply Ruff formatting to the conditional test

findings.description: Valid configs put the identifier in the top-level `identifier` string; `bundle` is an object (or omitted), so this lookup makes `original_identifier()` return `None`. Android/iOS dev and build calls to `write_options` fail with `app configuration is missing an identifier`, and the IDE scripts' `read_options` panics. Restore the `identifier` key.
findings.failureMode: Any valid mobile project fails to write the CLI options server address; invoking the IDE build script reaches read_options.expect and panics for the missing original identifier.
findings.title: Read the original identifier from `identifier`

findings.description: A file cannot have both `json` and `json5` extensions, so this `&&` disables schema validation for every JSON/JSON5 load and reload. For example, `productName: "bad/name"` violates the bundled schema's filename pattern but still deserializes as `Config`; the loader now accepts it instead of reporting the schema error and exiting. Restore `||` so either format is validated.
findings.failureMode: Loading tauri.conf.json with productName bad/name returns a Config and continues instead of rejecting the schema violation.
findings.title: Keep schema validation enabled for either JSON format

findings.description: This replaces `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;` with a metadata-only insertion, leaving the merged `value` unused. With a cached `productName: "old-name"` and an override of `"new-name"`, `merge_with` returns success and sets `TAURI_CONFIG` to the new value, but the returned handle still exposes the old name. Restore deserialization and assignment to `inner` alongside the metadata update.
findings.failureMode: merge_with succeeds but leaves ConfigHandle.inner unchanged, so Rust config readers and TAURI_CONFIG consumers see different configuration values.
findings.title: Update the cached config after merging overrides

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reports this added statement and exits 1 because rustfmt splits the `.expect(...)` onto a continuation line. This fails the repository's mandatory Rust formatting check and the `rustfmt` CI job. Apply rustfmt to this statement.
findings.failureMode: The rustfmt CI job exits nonzero on the new schema-loading statement.
findings.title: Format the schema-loading statement with rustfmt

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` also reports this new insertion: rustfmt requires the chained `.extensions.insert(...)` to be split across lines. Even after formatting the schema loader, this statement still makes the mandatory formatting check and `rustfmt` CI job fail. Apply rustfmt to this insertion.
findings.failureMode: The rustfmt CI job independently exits nonzero on the new metadata insertion statement.
findings.title: Format the extension insertion with rustfmt

findings.description: The rewrite supplies seven objects but passes argc=6, so newobj is omitted and every successful HINCRBYFLOAT propagates HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field without its required value. HSETEX rejects it: replicas skip the update, and default-policy AOF replay loses the acknowledged increment (reproduced as 2.1 reverting to 1). With propagation-error-behavior=panic, replay instead aborts the server. Pass 7 as the argument count.
findings.failureMode: The missing value produces an invalid replicated/AOF command, losing acknowledged HINCRBYFLOAT updates during failover or AOF replay and crashing receivers configured to panic on propagation errors.
findings.title: Pass all seven arguments to the HSETEX rewrite

findings.description: Removing HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes HINCRBYFLOAT clear an existing field expiration on the primary. For HSETEX h1 EX 100 FIELDS 1 f1 1 followed by HINCRBYFLOAT h1 f1 1.1, HTTL changes from 100 to -1 in both listpackex and hashtable encodings, so the field never expires. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL in this local update independently of the replication rewrite.
findings.failureMode: An increment of an unexpired field drops its expiration on the primary and makes the field persistent.
findings.title: Retain the field TTL when incrementing on the primary

findings.description: Removing static exports addHashFieldToReply even though every caller is in t_hash.c. This introduces a globally visible internal symbol and violates AGENTS.md rule 7. Retain static on this definition.
findings.failureMode: A file-local implementation helper becomes an externally visible symbol, violating the repository's mandatory encapsulation rule.
findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

findings.description: Renaming this test to `verify...` removes XCTest's required `test` prefix (also mandated by repository rule 6). Running the share-long-press suite no longer executes the bookmarked-URL Reminders assertions, so a broken bookmark-to-Reminders share flow silently passes. Restore the `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` entry point.
findings.failureMode: XCTest no longer discovers the previously executable bookmarked-URL Reminders test.
findings.title: Keep the Reminders test discoverable by XCTest

findings.description: The `iPad()` condition suppresses the Light reset for all iPad tests, but `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` still selects Dark there. Theme preferences are unprefixed `UserDefaults.standard` values; `ClearProfile` clears only profile-prefixed settings. Later onboarding runs therefore inherit Dark, including a preselected Dark appearance card, rather than the restored Light configuration. Preserve the theme reset for iPad tests that change appearance.
findings.failureMode: An iPad dark-mode onboarding test leaves persistent Dark theme selection, contaminating later light-mode test runs even when the profile is cleared.
findings.title: Restore the theme after the iPad dark-mode tour

findings.description: On iOS 17+, every iPad onboarding test and the iPhone bottom-placement test return before `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. The base teardown also terminates the app, so both cleanup paths are bypassed and the tested application is left running after the case instead of being released. Skip only the theme-reset call and always execute lifecycle cleanup.
findings.failureMode: The tested application is left running after affected test cases because neither the local nor base termination executes.
findings.title: Skip theme navigation without skipping teardown

findings.description: A reader-mode tap dispatches showReaderMode, but this now routes to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which saves the page instead of enabling or disabling reader mode. Summarizer long-press and VoiceOver magic tap also use this action. On a private tab, an ordinary reader-mode tap now persists the private URL and title in the profile's ReadingList.db without a save request, leaving them visible after the private tab is closed. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.failureMode: Reader-mode taps save pages rather than toggle reader mode; on private tabs the wrong operation permanently exposes private URLs/titles in the shared reading-list database.
findings.title: Keep reader-mode taps out of the reading-list action

findings.description: This switch runs before dispatching showReaderMode, so .available must yield true for the requested enabled state, while .active must yield false. Inverting it also changes the emitted privacy flag because the existing ToolbarTelemetry helper assigns isEnabled to the isPrivate extra: normal-reader exits are now recorded as private, and private-reader entries as non-private. The default nil-state path also fails testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes. Restore .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: The inverted argument newly misclassifies normal exits/private entries in emitted telemetry and makes the existing middleware test fail.
findings.title: Restore the reader-mode telemetry state mapping

findings.description: For a reader-mode tab, selectedTab.url is the internal http://localhost/.../reader-mode/page?url=... URL, while AddressBarState contains the decoded article URL. This condition now passes the raw internal URL into cancelEdit, overwriting that state when Cancel, Menu or Tabs is tapped. LocationView does not decode it, so the address bar shows localhost and subsequent editing exposes the internal URL. Restore the reader-URL exclusion so the reducer retains its existing display URL.
findings.failureMode: Tapping Cancel, Menu or Tabs on a reader-mode page replaces the article's address with localhost and the internal reader URL.
findings.title: Preserve the article URL when cancelling reader-mode editing

findings.description: Removing private makes the injected GleanWrapper accessible to every Client caller and drops its explicit access modifier. This widens an implementation detail into module API, violating repository mandate 11, which requires private implementation details and explicit access control. Keep private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: The Glean dependency becomes accessible outside ToolbarTelemetry contrary to the repository's mandatory access-control contract.
findings.title: Retain private access for the telemetry dependency

findings.description: SelectLightTheme taps lightThemeView. ThemeSelectionView marks exactly the selected option as selected, and GenericImageOption exposes that state as "1" or "0". Reading darkThemeView here therefore yields "0" after selecting Light and makes testCheckSystemThemeChanges fail on a correct app. Restore lightThemeView for this assertion.
findings.failureMode: Running testCheckSystemThemeChanges selects Light but asserts the Dark option is selected, producing a false test failure.
findings.title: Read the Light selection after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving goto(NewTabScreen) after the Done tap leaves the test on TopSitesSettingsViewController, which has no Done button. Done is installed on the parent Homepage/main Settings screens, so waitAndTap now times out before reaching the final assertions. Restore the navigation/back step before tapping Done.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection tries to tap a nonexistent Done button on the Shortcuts screen and fails on the normal execution path.
findings.title: Leave Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result`, but this helper now returns `FileWriteError` and every caller still uses `?`. The bundler's `Error` has no `From<FileWriteError>` conversion, so Linux builds fail with E0277 at all five calls. Preserve the helper's original `std::io::Result<()>` error type while borrowing the byte slice.
findings.failureMode: Compiling tauri-bundler on Linux fails because ? cannot convert FileWriteError into crate::Error.
findings.title: Keep the helper error convertible to the bundler error

findings.description: Every missing-tool branch calls this helper with a path that does not exist. `fs::set_permissions` now runs before `fs::write`, so it returns NotFound and prevents creation of AppRun, linuxdeploy, and the plugin files. Write the file first, then set its executable permissions as before.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling in a fresh or partially populated cache fails with NotFound before a missing tool can be created.
findings.title: Write the tool before setting its permissions

findings.description: When the tools cache lacks `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh`, the new `gtk.exists()` condition skips writing the bundled script. Even if every other tool is already cached, `bundle_project` still unconditionally requests `--plugin gtk`, so linuxdeploy fails with `Could not find plugin: gtk`. Restore `!gtk.exists()` so missing plugins are created.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling with an empty cache omits the required GTK plugin and linuxdeploy fails plugin discovery.
findings.title: Create the GTK plugin when it is missing

findings.description: The new `FileWriteError` manually implements `Display` and `Error` instead of deriving `thiserror::Error` with variant messages, violating mandatory repository rule 8 for custom error enums. Use the required derive and `#[error(...)]` attributes.
findings.failureMode: The newly added custom error enum fails the repository's mandatory structured-error compliance requirement.
findings.title: Derive the new error with thiserror

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this added line: the project's formatter wraps `.map_err(FileWriteError::Permissions)` onto a continuation line. Apply rustfmt so the change satisfies mandatory formatting rule 3.
findings.failureMode: The required cargo fmt check exits unsuccessfully on the changed permission-setting statement.
findings.title: Format the new permission-setting call with rustfmt

findings.description: This new source file uses four-space block indentation (including these lines) rather than the two spaces required by `.editorconfig` and mandatory rule 6. It fails the repository's source-format compliance requirement; reindent the script to the required width.
findings.failureMode: The new GTK script violates the mandatory EditorConfig indentation requirement.
findings.title: Use the mandated two-space indentation in the GTK script

findings.description: This new source file uses four-space block indentation (including this line) rather than the two spaces required by `.editorconfig` and mandatory rule 6. It fails the repository's source-format compliance requirement; reindent the script to the required width.
findings.failureMode: The new GStreamer script violates the mandatory EditorConfig indentation requirement.
findings.title: Use the mandated two-space indentation in the GStreamer script

findings.description: The rewrite passes seven objects but declares argc as 6, so newobj is omitted and every successful HINCRBYFLOAT propagates `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` without a value. Replicas reject the update; AOF replay silently loses it with the default error policy, or panics when configured to do so. An AOF restart reproduced the value reverting from 2.1 to 1. Pass 7 to retain the final value.
findings.failureMode: Every successful HINCRBYFLOAT writes an invalid command into replication/AOF. Confirmed default AOF restart loses updates; propagation error panic makes replay or replicas crash.
findings.title: Use seven arguments for the rewritten HSETEX command

findings.description: Removing HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL makes HINCRBYFLOAT clear an existing field expiration on the master. After `HSETEX h EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1; HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1.1`, the field becomes persistent instead of retaining its deadline; a correctly rewritten KEEPTTL replica would still expire it. Restore HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this hashTypeSet call.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on an expiring field removes its expiry on the master, retaining stale fields and diverging from replicas once the command count is corrected.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the master as well

findings.description: addHashFieldToReply is called only within t_hash.c, but this change removes static and exports an internal implementation symbol. This violates the mandatory file-local helper rule and adds unnecessary external linkage. Restore static on this definition.
findings.failureMode: The production object now exposes an internal helper as a global symbol in violation of the repository's required encapsulation rule.
findings.title: Keep the file-local reply helper static

findings.description: For a valid config such as `{"identifier":"com.example.app","bundle":{}}`, `bundle.as_str()` is None. All Android/iOS dev/build commands then fail in `write_options` with `app configuration is missing an identifier`; direct IDE build-script calls panic in `read_options`'s `.expect("failed to read CLI options")`. Restore the lookup of the top-level `identifier` key.
findings.failureMode: Every valid mobile config loses its original_identifier, causing mobile command errors and a reachable panic in read_options.
findings.title: Preserve the top-level original identifier

findings.description: No path can have both `json` and `json5` extensions, so this `&&` makes schema validation unreachable. For example, `productName: "bad/name"` is rejected by the bundled schema but accepted by Serde: the base loader exits 1 while the new loader accepts it without diagnostics. Restore `||` so schema-only constraints remain enforced.
findings.failureMode: JSON/JSON5 configuration validation is skipped, accepting schema-invalid values such as a product name containing a slash.
findings.title: Restore validation for JSON and JSON5 configs

findings.description: The deleted assignment `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?;` applied and validated the merged config. Now the merged `value` is discarded: after loading a config without `build.devUrl` and calling `merge_with` with a new URL, the returned handle still reports None while `TAURI_CONFIG` contains the URL. Restore the assignment as well as tracking the extension.
findings.failureMode: merge_with returns stale in-memory configuration while exporting changed configuration to subprocesses.
findings.title: Apply merged values to the cached config

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this new line because rustfmt splits the chained `.expect(...)` call. This violates repository mandate 3 and fails the rustfmt CI job; apply the project rustfmt layout.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory cargo fmt check exits 1 on the newly added schema parse statement.
findings.title: Format the bundled-schema parsing statement

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` independently fails on this new line: rustfmt puts `config_metadata`, `.extensions`, and `.insert(...)` on separate lines. This violates repository mandate 3 and fails the rustfmt CI job; format this call too.
findings.failureMode: The mandatory cargo fmt check still exits 1 on the extension insertion after only formatting the schema parse statement.
findings.title: Format the extension insertion chain

findings.description: The helper now returns `FileWriteError`, but `prepare_tools` still returns `crate::Result` and propagates all helper calls with `?`. `crate::Error` has no `From<FileWriteError>` implementation, so Linux builds fail with E0277. Map the helper errors into the existing bundler error type.
findings.failureMode: Compiling the Linux AppImage module fails because ? cannot convert FileWriteError into crate::Error.
findings.title: Preserve conversion into the bundler error type

findings.description: Every initial tool installation passes a nonexistent destination, but `set_permissions` now runs before `fs::write` creates it. This returns NotFound and prevents first-time AppImage bundling, including installation of the embedded GStreamer script. Restore write-before-chmod ordering.
findings.failureMode: When an AppRun, linuxdeploy, GStreamer or output-plugin cache file is absent, its installation aborts with NotFound before creating it.
findings.title: Write tool files before setting their permissions

findings.description: When the GTK plugin is absent from an otherwise populated tools cache, `gtk.exists()` is false and the embedded script is never written. `bundle_project` always requests `--plugin gtk`, so on a machine without a separately installed GTK plugin, linuxdeploy fails and no AppImage is produced. Restore `if !gtk.exists()` to install the missing plugin.
findings.failureMode: AppImage bundling with no cached GTK plugin skips its installation and linuxdeploy fails to resolve --plugin gtk.
findings.title: Create the GTK plugin when it is missing

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this new line, which rustfmt splits before `.map_err`. Mandate 3 requires the formatting check to pass. Apply the project's rustfmt output.
findings.failureMode: The repository-mandated cargo fmt --all -- --check exits with a formatting diff on the added permissions line.
findings.title: Format the permissions call with the project rustfmt configuration

findings.description: The new `FileWriteError` manually implements `Display` and `Error`, violating mandate 8, which requires `thiserror::Error` and descriptive `#[error]` attributes on custom error enums. Replace the manual implementations with the required derive.
findings.failureMode: The new error enum fails the mandatory repository structured-error compliance rule.
findings.title: Derive the new error type with thiserror

findings.description: This newly added source file uses four-space indentation here and throughout its function bodies, contrary to mandate 6 and `.editorconfig`, which require two spaces for all source files. Reindent the script to meet the mandatory formatting contract.
findings.failureMode: The new GTK source file does not satisfy the repository's mandatory EditorConfig formatting standards.
findings.title: Use the required two-space indentation in the GTK script

findings.description: This newly added source file uses four-space indentation here and throughout its function bodies, contrary to mandate 6 and `.editorconfig`, which require two spaces for all source files. Reindent the script to meet the mandatory formatting contract.
findings.failureMode: The new GStreamer source file does not satisfy the repository's mandatory EditorConfig formatting standards.
findings.title: Use the required two-space indentation in the GStreamer script

findings.description: The guard permits None, so rendered remains str | None at return despite the declared -> str. Running basedpyright 1.31.7 with api/pyrightconfig.json reports reportReturnType at line 40, causing the registered type-check to fail. Reject every non-string value (including None) with TemplateRenderError before returning.
findings.failureMode: The new adapter's normal type-check fails because a nullable result is returned from a method declared to return str. The default Jinja transformer always returns a string, so the hypothesized runtime crash was pre-existing for malformed responses and is not the finding.
findings.title: Reject None to satisfy the renderer's string return type

findings.description: The factory computes node_class from the registry and requested version, but this new branch always instantiates TemplateTransformNode. When a template-node subclass/version is registered via Node's existing registry, configurations selecting it now execute the built-in v1 implementation instead. Inject the renderer into the selected node_class rather than bypassing version dispatch.
findings.failureMode: A currently supported externally registered template node with version 2 is selected by the registry lookup but discarded; create_node returns the v1 node and produces v1 output instead of the registered implementation's output.
findings.title: Instantiate the selected template node version

findings.description: A renderer implementing __bool__ as False or __len__ returning zero still satisfies Jinja2TemplateRenderer, but this expression silently discards it and invokes CodeExecutor instead. The factory repeats the same fallback at node_factory.py:63. Test for None explicitly at both sites so an injected renderer is always used.
findings.failureMode: An explicitly supplied renderer whose truth value is False is ignored, so a node unexpectedly uses the sandbox renderer and returns its output or sandbox-unavailable error instead of the requested custom rendering.
findings.title: Preserve explicitly supplied falsey renderers

findings.description: The new assertion triggers SIM300 under api/.ruff.toml. Ruff 0.14.0 reports this as the only check error in the changed files, so make check fails. Put result.outputs['output'] on the left and the expected string on the right.
findings.failureMode: The registered make check command fails with SIM300 on the newly added mixed-type-list test assertion.
findings.title: Use the lint-required operand order in the new assertion

findings.description: The new calls for dotnet-eng-internal (here) and dotnet-tools-internal (line 184) add these feeds to PackageSources. If a valid existing credential element puts ClearTextPassword on the same line as its opening feed tag, the later credential-existence grep prints the whole element to stdout, leaking the stored token into logs. The base script does not print these credentials. Make that grep quiet or redirect it to /dev/null before adding the new feeds to its processing list.
findings.failureMode: A credentialed invocation with an existing compact dotnet-eng-internal or dotnet-tools-internal credential element writes its clear-text token to the build log; these feeds were not processed by the base script.
findings.title: Avoid logging existing credentials for the new internal feeds

findings.description: The patch comparison is inverted. This first servicing build still uses the 9.0.0 baseline, which lists System.Text.Json for Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup although its current project no longer references it. With patch 1 the new condition raises BUILD002 and stops restore/build; with patch 2 it disables the dependency-removal guard altogether. Use != '1' so the transition patch is exempt and subsequent servicing patches are checked.
findings.failureMode: The current 10.0.1 build fails BUILD002 on AzureAppServices.HostingStartup's old System.Text.Json baseline dependency; subsequent patches silently skip removed-dependency validation.
findings.title: Exempt patch 1 rather than checking only patch 1

findings.description: Both macOS pools now use macOS-15, but their mandatory setup commands (lines 166 and 392) still select /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer. The new image does not include that installation, so xcode-select fails before the build runs. Update both commands to the installed Xcode 16.4 path, not just their display names.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs stop at xcode-select with an invalid developer directory after the image upgrade.
findings.title: Select an Xcode installation available on macOS 15

findings.description: The new block-scoped namespace triggers IDE0161, configured as a warning in .editorconfig. CSharp.Common.targets enables code-style analysis and the generated build props treat warnings as errors, so building the Components E2E project now fails. This also violates mandate 2. Restore the semicolon namespace and remove the enclosing braces.
findings.failureMode: A Components E2E build with the repository's default code-style and warnings-as-errors settings fails with IDE0161.
findings.title: Keep the file-scoped namespace to avoid IDE0161

findings.description: WorkflowRun inputs/outputs are serialized with json.dumps, which stores CJK text as Unicode escapes. Passing the raw keyword to escape_like_pattern makes a search for '中文' return no logs even when inputs/outputs contain that text. JSON-encode the keyword for the inputs/outputs predicates before LIKE-escaping it, keeping a plain-text pattern for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Workflow log keyword searches no longer find runs containing non-ASCII input/output text serialized with json.dumps defaults.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding in workflow log searches

findings.description: Connections set cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote', so the two backslashes in the emitted ESCAPE '\\' SQL are not reduced to one. The fallback LIKE query consequently supplies a two-character escape string and fails rather than returning documents. Emit one backslash in the SQL literal under quote mode.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta full-text search fallback fails with an invalid ESCAPE literal for connections configured in quote mode.
findings.title: Use a single-character ClickZetta ESCAPE literal

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper emits backslash escapes but the SQL declares '|'. Searching for '50%' sends '%50\%%', which requires a literal backslash instead of matching '50%'; matching documents are omitted. Declare backslash as the SQL escape character to match the helper.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback LIKE searches for percent, underscore or backslash omit actual matching documents because the SQL escape character differs from the helper's.
findings.title: Match IRIS's escape character to the helper

findings.description: The 'not contains' branch escapes values with backslashes but omits escape='\\'. On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES enabled there is no default LIKE escape, so 'not contains %' incorrectly includes metadata containing '%' because it tests for a literal backslash followed by a wildcard. Pass escape='\\' to notlike, as in the adjacent LIKE branches.
findings.failureMode: On MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, escaped NOT LIKE filters incorrectly include documents that contain the literal substring meant to be excluded.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for NOT LIKE too

findings.description: The patch-1 servicing build still uses the 9.0.0 baseline. This equality therefore makes Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup fail reference resolution with BUILD002 for System.Text.Json, which that baseline lists but the net10.0 project no longer references. It also disables dependency-removal validation for patch 2 and later. Change the patch gate to != '1' so the initial transition is exempt while subsequent servicing patches retain validation.
findings.failureMode: First servicing build fails BUILD002 for System.Text.Json in AzureAppServices.HostingStartup; later patches disable dependency-removal guard
findings.title: Invert the first-patch dependency validation gate

findings.description: Both macOS pool changes (lines 106 and 323) leave the setup commands at lines 166 and 392 selecting /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app. The macOS-15 hosted image does not contain that Xcode, so xcode-select exits nonzero and all macOS jobs stop before building. Update both commands to the installed Xcode 16.4 path rather than only their display names.
findings.failureMode: macOS-15 jobs fail at Xcode selection before build
findings.title: Select an Xcode installed on macOS-15

findings.description: Replacing the file-scoped namespace with a block-scoped declaration violates mandatory AGENTS.md rule 2 and the repository's file_scoped editorconfig setting. Style verification of this file emits IDE0161 and exits nonzero. Restore the semicolon declaration and remove the new enclosing braces; the quarantine attribute does not require this namespace change.
findings.failureMode: File-scoped namespace compliance and style verification fail with IDE0161
findings.title: Retain the required file-scoped namespace

findings.description: When tab swiping is enabled, the right skeleton starts at the container's trailing edge and is containerWidth - 32 points wide. This change attaches the active toolbar's leading and trailing edges to that skeleton in reverse order: a 390-point container now demands a -358-point toolbar width instead of 390. The resulting invalid layout collapses or misplaces the active address bar. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor as the leading constraint target.
findings.failureMode: Enabling tab swiping creates contradictory horizontal constraints and breaks the active toolbar layout.
findings.title: Restore the toolbar's leading attachment to the left skeleton

findings.description: On first configuring a web page, updateActionStack sets new trailing buttons (reload/stop, reader mode or summarize) to alpha 0. This list now repeats browserActionStack and omits trailingPageActionStack, so neither animation branch restores those buttons to alpha 1; they remain invisible and unavailable to touch. Replace the final term with trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page-action buttons remain at alpha 0 instead of becoming visible.
findings.title: Restore trailing action buttons in the alpha update

findings.description: For a supported .default() UX configuration (4-point divider), trailing-only page actions now receive a zero-width divider, while leading-only actions add a divider after the location text despite having no trailing buttons. The divider is constrained next to trailingPageActionStack, not the leading stack. Base hasPageActions on trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews to preserve the configured spacing.
findings.failureMode: The divider spacing next to trailing page actions is removed, or added when there are no trailing actions.
findings.title: Base the trailing divider on trailing page actions

findings.description: An authenticated regular `MEMBER` can POST to this endpoint and receive a usable shareable invite link: `RolesGuard` treats `TEAM_MEMBER` as the minimum role, and `TeamService.createInvite` has no admin check. This bypasses the admin-only invite permission enforced by the existing invite handler and contradicts the added 403 test. Require `TEAM_ADMIN`.
findings.failureMode: An authenticated MEMBER posts to the invite endpoint and gains an invite link without admin authorization.
findings.title: Require team admin to create invitations

findings.description: Production `start:prod` on Node 20 crashes while loading the new controller: the Nest build leaves this as `require("@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService")`, but the features workspace only has `teamService.ts` at that path, so Node throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Import `TeamService` from the compiled `@calcom/platform-libraries` entry point, as the organization invite controller does.
findings.failureMode: Production API startup loads the newly wired controller and cannot resolve its raw features TypeScript import.
findings.title: Load TeamService from the built platform bundle

findings.description: New invitations return `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` instead of the random verification token. Repeated calls return the same `data.token`, it is not the token in `inviteLink`, and using it to retrieve/redeem an invitation fails. Return `token` or `newToken.token`.
findings.failureMode: A successful createInvite call returns a deterministic identifier as its token, which does not match any newly created verificationToken.token.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: For a regular team (`parentId: null`, `isOrganization: false`), the reversed condition now returns `/signup?token=...` instead of `/teams?token=...`. An already signed-in invitee is redirected from signup to `/` before the token is processed, so no membership is created. Conversely, organization invites now skip the signup/onboarding flow. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)`.
findings.failureMode: A signed-in existing user opens a newly created regular-team inviteLink and signup redirects them to the root without redeeming the invite.
findings.title: Keep regular-team invites out of organization signup

findings.description: XCTest discovers methods beginning with `test`; the renamed `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` has no callers and FeatureFlaggedTestBase adds no custom discovery. Full functional runs therefore stop exercising bookmark-to-Reminders sharing while still passing. Restore the original `test`-prefixed name so this scenario remains discoverable.
findings.failureMode: XCTest does not discover the renamed bookmark-to-Reminders test, silently removing active coverage from UI test runs.
findings.title: Restore the test prefix for bookmark Reminders coverage

findings.description: On iPad/iOS 17+, `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` still explicitly selects Dark, but this blanket `iPad()` exception now prevents restoring Light. Theme settings live in unprefixed UserDefaults.standard keys; ClearProfile only clears profile-prefixed preferences, so the next launch retains Dark and subsequent onboarding preselects the dark theme. Exempt only the skipped bottom-placement case, not all iPad tests.
findings.failureMode: Running the dark-mode onboarding test on iPad leaves persistent theme preferences set to Dark for subsequent UI tests.
findings.title: Restore the theme after the iPad dark-mode test

findings.description: On iOS 17+, all iPad onboarding tests and the iPhone bottom-placement test return before both `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()`. BaseTestCase's teardown is also responsible for terminating the app, so these cases leave the launched application running when teardown returns, including when the iPad test is skipped. Skip only theme restoration and always execute the remaining cleanup.
findings.failureMode: After an affected test finishes or skips, its explicit application cleanup is bypassed and the launched app remains running.
findings.title: Do not return before shared teardown

findings.description: The standard Nest CommonJS build preserves this as require('@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService'), but @calcom/features ships teamService.ts without a matching .js entry or runtime loader. Since TeamsInviteModule is loaded at startup, start:prod fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the import also violates API v2's Biome restriction. Import TeamService from @calcom/platform-libraries, which already exports the bundled service.
findings.failureMode: API v2 production startup crashes resolving an unbundled TypeScript-only workspace subpath.
findings.title: Use the bundled TeamService export in API v2

findings.description: An authenticated user whose team membership is MEMBER passes RolesGuard with this minimum role, and TeamService.createInvite performs no additional authorization. The user can therefore mint and share valid invitation links despite the admin-only contract (and the new non-admin test receives success instead of 403). Change the decorator to TEAM_ADMIN.
findings.failureMode: Regular team members can mint invitations that admit other users, bypassing admin-only authorization.
findings.title: Require team admin privileges to generate invites

findings.description: This route accepts organization sub-team IDs but omits the Admin API entitlement check used by the existing organization invite route. An admin in a non-platform organization with Admin API access disabled can obtain a valid invitation through `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite`, while `/v2/organizations/:orgId/teams/:teamId/invite` rejects the same operation. Resolve the team's organization and enforce its Admin API entitlement for organization contexts.
findings.failureMode: Organizations without Admin API access can bypass the existing organization invite entitlement check through the new team-only URL.
findings.title: Preserve Admin API gating for organization invites

findings.description: New invitations now return `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` rather than the random value stored in VerificationToken.token and embedded in inviteLink. Thus repeated requests return identical tokens, the new E2E assertions fail, and redeeming or reusing data.token yields 'Invite not found'. Return newToken.token (or the generated token) instead.
findings.failureMode: New invite returns a non-redeemable, constant identifier instead of the secret token.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: The inverted condition routes standalone-team invites to `/signup` and organization/sub-team invites to `/teams`. For an already logged-in standalone-team invitee, signup's getServerSideProps immediately redirects to `/`, discarding the token instead of creating the pending membership via the teams page. Organization invitees also lose their signup/onboarding flow. Restore `if (!isOrgContext)`.
findings.failureMode: Logged-in standalone-team invitees are redirected home without joining; organization invite links no longer route through organization signup.
findings.title: Restore the organization-context link branch

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, the test now reads darkThemeView and expects its value to be "1". A correctly selected light theme leaves the dark button unselected ("0"), so testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails on a correct app. Read lightThemeView here, as before.
findings.failureMode: Running testCheckSystemThemeChanges with a correctly functioning appearance selector produces an assertion failure immediately after selecting Light, because the asserted value is taken from the Dark button.
findings.title: Read the light-theme button after selecting Light

findings.description: Moving `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` below the Done tap leaves the app on the Shortcuts subpage when `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()` executes. That page is TopSitesSettingsViewController, which has no Done item; Done is installed by the Homepage and main Settings controllers. The test now times out before reaching the section assertions. Restore navigation out of Shortcuts before tapping Done.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection pushes TopSitesSettingsViewController, toggles Shortcuts, and now waits for a Done button that does not exist on that subpage; previously the preceding navigator.goto popped out of Shortcuts first.
findings.title: Leave Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: MagicLink.js remains under services/lib/magic-link; this PR does not rename it. Loading MembersAPI now throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link, preventing the members service and Ghost startup. Restore the import to ../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink.
findings.failureMode: Loading MembersAPI throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the changed MagicLink import.
findings.title: Keep the existing MagicLink module path

findings.description: EmailEventStorage.js is not renamed in this PR. During normal Ghost boot, emailAnalytics.init() now requires nonexistent ../email-service/email-event-storage and throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND, aborting startup. Restore the import to ../email-service/EmailEventStorage.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the EmailEventStorage require.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventStorage module path

findings.description: EmailEventProcessor.js is not renamed in this PR. Even after restoring the preceding storage import, emailAnalytics.init() independently throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../email-service/email-event-processor, aborting Ghost startup. Restore the import to ../email-service/EmailEventProcessor.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization independently throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the EmailEventProcessor require.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventProcessor module path

findings.description: Availability.days is Int[] in Prisma and getScheduleListItemData expects number[]. Declaring it string[] makes ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper's call to that transformer fail type checking after useAtomGetAllSchedules switches to this type. Restore days: number[].
findings.failureMode: TypeScript build/type-check failure in ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper.
findings.title: Keep availability weekdays numeric

findings.description: The upstream IFromUser.id is number, but the local copy changes it to string. EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes useAvailableSlots().data to useAvailableTimeSlots, which requires IGetAvailableSlots, so this mismatch produces a TypeScript error (and also affects Booker's schedule prop). Restore id: number.
findings.failureMode: CalendarView and Booker schedule consumers reject the new response type.
findings.title: Preserve the numeric out-of-office user ID

findings.description: Slot.userIds was number[] before the move, and the upstream slot types still use numeric IDs. Changing it to string[] also changes onTimeslotsLoaded: a previously valid callback accepting slots with userIds?: number[] now fails type checking. This refactor should preserve userIds?: number[].
findings.failureMode: Previously valid numeric onTimeslotsLoaded consumers no longer type-check.
findings.title: Preserve numeric slot user IDs

findings.description: validateCreateScheduleInput({name: "Work", schedule: 42, eventTypeId: "bad"}) returns successfully as CreateScheduleInput even though both optional fields violate that type. The existing create.schema.ts validates nested dates and numeric eventTypeId; use a typed local Zod schema to validate the whole object rather than casting after checking only name.
findings.failureMode: Invalid optional fields are accepted as a validated CreateScheduleInput.
findings.title: Validate optional fields before asserting the input type

findings.description: The new @calcom/trpc/** restriction also bans QueryCell imports still present in ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx:12 and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx:6. Biome lint now emits noRestrictedImports errors for these files. Migrate both remaining consumers when enabling this restriction.
findings.failureMode: New noRestrictedImports errors on existing atoms consumers.
findings.title: Migrate the remaining imports before widening the ban

findings.description: Calling validateCreateScheduleInput(null) throws a plain Error with no typed code, so consumers cannot categorize the validation failure. This violates AGENTS.md rule 10's explicit prohibition on generic Error objects. Use the repository's coded error hierarchy for this branch.
findings.failureMode: Invalid-object validation exposes an uncategorized generic Error.
findings.title: Use a coded error for invalid input objects

findings.description: Calling validateCreateScheduleInput({name: ""}) throws a plain Error with no typed code, so consumers cannot categorize the validation failure. AGENTS.md rule 10 explicitly prohibits generic Error objects. Use the repository's coded error hierarchy for this branch too.
findings.failureMode: Invalid-name validation exposes an uncategorized generic Error.
findings.title: Use a coded error for invalid schedule names

findings.description: The single-quoted 'object' literal conflicts with the mandated Biome quoteStyle: double configuration. Biome format reports an error for this new line; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: New object check fails the mandated Biome formatting check.
findings.title: Format the object type check with Biome

findings.description: The single-quoted error message conflicts with the mandated Biome quoteStyle: double configuration. Biome format reports an error for this new line; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: New invalid-object message fails the mandated Biome formatting check.

findings.description: The single-quoted 'string' literal conflicts with the mandated Biome quoteStyle: double configuration. Biome format reports an error for this new line; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: New name check fails the mandated Biome formatting check.
findings.title: Format the name type check with Biome

findings.description: The single-quoted error message conflicts with the mandated Biome quoteStyle: double configuration. Biome format reports an error for this new line; use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: New invalid-name message fails the mandated Biome formatting check.
findings.title: Format the invalid-name message with Biome

findings.description: Disabling strict also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. With the repository-locked dependency versions, tsc -b --noEmit now fails across the UI with 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json' and invalid route-param types; changing only this setting back to true makes the check pass. Restore strict:true to unblock build/validation and preserve the mandatory strict checking gate.
findings.failureMode: Mainline type validation/build fail with the locked router version; changing strict back to true passes type validation.
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled so the UI builds

findings.description: PostureSelect labels Proactive as 'Stays in', but these selectors always populate expect. With the default threshold=1, Stays in Paused produces expect:[paused] and no after: the paused transition increments the bucket to 1, and proactive_evaluation deletes that satisfied bucket. If the resource remains paused without another transition, the automation never fires. Bind the selected status to after for Proactive and expect for Reactive in both this file and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36.
findings.failureMode: For a Proactive pool/queue status trigger with default threshold 1, the chosen status event counts as expected rather than starting the absence timer; the satisfied bucket is deleted and no action occurs when the resource stays in that status.
findings.title: Bind proactive pool and queue status to after

findings.description: Clearing the textarea produces [""] because split("\n") always returns at least one entry, so the undefined branch is unreachable. This passes Zod but becomes a nonempty backend expect set that matches no real event; an empty expect set instead matches any event. Special-case an empty textarea to store [] so clearing the field restores its initial matching behavior.
findings.failureMode: Typing then clearing the expected events changes the displayed empty field from wildcard matching to matching no real event.
findings.title: Normalize an empty custom event list

findings.description: These new Proactive interval inputs permit 1–9 seconds, and the wizard's Zod schema accepts them, although the backend explicitly rejects nonzero proactive within values below 10 seconds. Entering 5 therefore produces a supposedly valid trigger configuration that fails server validation. Require at least 10 in the input and posture-dependent validation; fix deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:99, work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:96, and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:96 as well.
findings.failureMode: The wizard accepts within=5 for a Proactive trigger but the backend rejects the generated configuration.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive interval minimum

findings.description: The new Number callbacks store fractional thresholds, and EventTriggerSchema only checks min(1). Entering 1.5 passes the wizard's Next validation but is rejected by the backend's integer threshold field. Native step validation does not protect this path: Next is type=button and unmounts the inputs before Save. Require integer thresholds in form validation; this also affects deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:81 and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:78.
findings.failureMode: A threshold of 1.5 passes Zod/Next, survives after the inputs unmount, and produces a backend-invalid trigger configuration.
findings.title: Reject fractional event thresholds

findings.description: parseInt truncates valid number-input exponent notation: entering or pasting 1e2 stores 1 rather than 100, and the controlled input overwrites the entered value. Use Number(e.target.value) or valueAsNumber like the other templates so the generated threshold reflects the supplied number.
findings.failureMode: Pasting the valid integer 1e2 into the work-pool threshold silently configures 1 instead of 100.
findings.title: Parse the entire numeric threshold

findings.description: FormControl wraps the non-DOM Select root, so its id and aria-describedby/aria-invalid never reach the combobox button. The Status label points to no control, breaking label focus and leaving the selector and its errors unassociated for assistive technology. Wrap SelectTrigger with FormControl instead; apply the same correction in work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:43–49 and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:43–49.
findings.failureMode: Status dropdowns are unlabeled to assistive technology, their labels cannot focus them, and validation descriptions are not wired to the controls.
findings.title: Apply form accessibility props to SelectTrigger

findings.description: `strict: false` disables `strictNullChecks`, which TanStack Router requires. The registered `validate:types` command now fails across the UI with `strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json` and route-parameter errors; the build also runs `tsc -b` and cannot reach Vite. Restore `strict: true`, which also preserves the mandated type-safety gate.
findings.failureMode: validate:types / npm run build fails because TanStack Router's createRouter type explicitly rejects configs without strictNullChecks, and disabling it also collapses route param types.
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled for TanStack Router

findings.description: Both this field and `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36` always write `expect`, although Proactive is labeled 'Stays in'. With 'Stays in Not Ready', threshold 1 and within 30, the Not Ready event satisfies the expectation and its bucket is discarded; no alert fires if the resource remains Not Ready. Bind Proactive status selections to `trigger.after`, as the deployment template does.
findings.failureMode: The identical unconditional expect binding in both pool and queue templates prevents Stays in alerts: the selected status event increments count rather than merely arming a timer, so proactive evaluation discards its bucket.
findings.title: Arm proactive pool and queue triggers on status entry

findings.description: Changing posture switches the status control between `expect` and `after` without clearing the old field. Select Enters Not Ready, then Stays in Not Ready: the form retains both `expect=[not-ready]` and `after=[not-ready]`. A later Ready event cannot satisfy this trigger, so it can alert even though the deployment left Not Ready before the interval expired. Reset or recompute the inactive event criteria on posture changes.
findings.failureMode: Configure Reactive Not Ready, switch to Proactive and reselect Not Ready. The hidden expect filter survives; the backend ignores a subsequent Ready transition and reports the deployment as having stayed Not Ready.
findings.title: Clear hidden event criteria when changing posture

findings.description: Splitting an empty textarea returns `[""]`, so the length check never clears `trigger.expect`. After a user types and deletes the event list, an apparently blank form submits an empty-string event filter, which matches no real events instead of the backend's any-event behavior for an empty list. Filter blank lines and send an empty list or undefined when no events remain.
findings.failureMode: Type a custom event and erase it, then save a Reactive trigger. The unchanged schema accepts expect=[""]; EventTrigger.expects returns false for every nonempty event, so the automation never reacts unlike an untouched empty field.
findings.title: Represent an empty custom event list as empty

findings.description: `parseInt` parses only a prefix of the number input: pasting the valid integer-valued input `1e2` stores and displays 1 rather than 100, producing the wrong threshold. This global call also fails the error-level Biome `useNumberNamespace` rule and blocks the lint job. Use `Number(e.target.value)` or `valueAsNumber`, consistently with the other templates.
findings.failureMode: A user pastes scientific notation 1e2 into the work pool threshold, a valid integer-valued number input; parseInt turns it into 1 and saves a one-event automation rather than a hundred-event automation.
findings.title: Parse the whole numeric threshold

findings.description: Here and in both work-pool/work-queue status components at lines 42–47, `FormControl` wraps Radix's non-DOM `Select` root. Its id and aria attributes never reach `SelectTrigger`, leaving every Status label unassociated and each combobox unnamed for screen readers. The rendered controls fail label/name queries. Wrap `SelectTrigger` with `FormControl` instead.
findings.failureMode: All three new Status dropdowns render unnamed comboboxes; their labels cannot focus them and assistive technology cannot identify the field.
findings.title: Attach status labels to the select buttons

findings.description: Replacing `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` drops the encoding needed for WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs. Production writers still use json.dumps() into text columns, so a run containing `你好` stores `\u4f60\u597d`; searching `你好` now returns zero logs. JSON-encode the trimmed keyword before LIKE escaping for these two columns, using a separate raw escaped pattern for EndUser.session_id.
findings.failureMode: Keyword search for Chinese workflow inputs or outputs no longer finds runs stored as ASCII-escaped JSON.
findings.title: Preserve JSON encoding for workflow log searches

findings.description: ClickZetta connections set cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode='quote', so backslashes in SQL literals are not unescaped. This Python string emits `ESCAPE '\\'` with two backslashes in the SQL literal, which is not a single escape character. Fallback searches now fail instead of returning documents. Use a one-backslash literal for the configured quote mode.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta LIKE fallback generates an invalid multi-character ESCAPE argument under the connection's configured literal mode.
findings.title: Emit a single-character ESCAPE in ClickZetta quote mode

findings.description: With IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, the helper emits backslash escapes but SQL declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Searching `50%` produces `%50\%%` and misses text containing `50%`; ordinary pipe queries also acquire escape semantics. Declare backslash as the SQL escape character so the generated pattern is interpreted correctly.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search returns missing or incorrect results for special-character queries.
findings.title: Match the IRIS ESCAPE character to the helper

findings.description: The `not contains` branch escapes its value but omits `escape="\\"`, unlike the other operators. On MySQL with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES enabled, LIKE has no default escape character, so `not contains '50%'` tests for a backslash-containing pattern and incorrectly includes a document whose metadata is `50% discount`. Pass the escape argument to notlike as well.
findings.failureMode: MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES metadata exclusion filters include documents that contain the excluded literal.
findings.title: Declare the escape character for NOT LIKE too

findings.description: updateToolbarLayout now includes browserActionStack twice and omits trailingPageActionStack. updateActionStack sets newly inserted buttons to alpha = 0, and neither ToolbarButton.configure nor its theme application restores that alpha. Opening a page or switching reload/stop controls therefore leaves the trailing buttons invisible and untappable, with or without animation. Include trailingPageActionStack in this list.
findings.failureMode: Initial toolbar configuration with trailing page actions leaves those buttons at alpha zero instead of displaying them.
findings.title: Restore trailing action button visibility

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, the toolbar's leading edge now targets the right skeleton's trailing edge, while its trailing edge still targets that skeleton's leading edge. Since the right skeleton has width containerWidth - 32 and sits beyond the container, this reverses the toolbar's horizontal bounds. A 390-point container produces a zero-width toolbar at x=390, hiding the address bar. Restore leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor as the leading target.
findings.failureMode: Constructing AddressToolbarContainer with swiping tabs enabled collapses and moves the main toolbar offscreen.
findings.title: Keep the toolbar's leading edge on the left skeleton

findings.description: locationDividerView is between locationView and trailingPageActionStack, but its width now depends on leadingPageActionStack. With the supported .default() UX configuration (4-point divider), trailing-only actions lose their divider and leading-only actions gain an unwanted divider after the URL. Check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews instead.
findings.failureMode: Configurations with different leading and trailing action occupancy render the divider and spacing incorrectly.
findings.title: Base trailing divider spacing on trailing actions

findings.description: The module remains services/lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js; no magic-link.js was added or renamed. Node resolution of this new path throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND while loading MembersAPI through members/api.js, preventing Ghost startup. Restore the import to MagicLink.
findings.failureMode: MembersAPI require fails synchronously with MODULE_NOT_FOUND due to a nonexistent kebab-case MagicLink module.
findings.title: Import MagicLink using its unchanged filename

findings.description: Ghost boot calls emailAnalytics.init(), which now throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND because the module is still named email-service/EmailEventStorage.js. Node resolution confirms the new kebab-case path does not exist. Restore the matching import to prevent startup failure.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization/startup throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../email-service/email-event-storage.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventStorage import

findings.description: After fixing the preceding storage import, Ghost boot still fails in emailAnalytics.init(): the processor module remains email-service/EmailEventProcessor.js, so this new path throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Restore the matching import; correcting the storage path alone does not fix startup.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for ../email-service/email-event-processor independently of the storage import.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventProcessor import
